stories.text: The tunnel was meant to let carriages from the Park reach Derby Road through the sandstone. It was begun in about 1844 and finished by T. C. Hine in 1855–56, but at 1 in 12 it was too steep for horses and carriages, so it became a footway.[^walk] It runs from Tunnel Road to Derby Road, with steps halfway up to Upper College Street.

73655.sum: The Park Tunnel is a residential building on Park Terrace. The building was built in 1881, according to OpenStreetMap, though other sources give a different date. It is Grade II listed as Numbers 18, 19 and 20 and Attached Railings and Retaining Wall to Park Tunnel and was designed by Thomas Chambers Hine.

stories.text: Tower House is one of the earliest houses in the Park, built to P. F. Robinson's designs between 1827 and 1833.[^walk] Watson Fothergill later gave it the tower that names it.[^walk] It is listed Grade II.

73964.sum: Tower House is a residential building on Park Row. The building was built in 1827, according to OpenStreetMap. It is Grade II listed and was designed by Watson Fothergill.

stories.text: The 8th Duke of Newcastle sold the Park in 1938 to the Nuffield Trust, which passed it on to Oxford University. The estate became a conservation area in 1969, and talks that began in 1986 between the residents' association and the university put the estate in the hands of its residents, who run it from the Estate Office.
stories.nm: Sold, saved and run by its residents

74029.sum: Park Estate Office is an office building on Lenton Road. The building was built in 1909, according to OpenStreetMap. It is Grade II listed and was designed by Arthur Richard Calvert.
